question: Explain the Test-Driven Development (TDD) cycle. What are the benefits and challenges of practicing TDD?

keyPoints: TDD cycle: Red (write failing test) → Green (write minimal code to pass) → Refactor (improve code)
Benefits: better design, higher confidence, executable documentation, fewer bugs
Challenges: initial slowdown, learning curve, requires discipline, can be difficult for exploratory work
TDD drives better architecture: forces thinking about interfaces, encourages loose coupling
Not appropriate for all scenarios: UI, prototypes, unclear requirements
expectedAnswer.explanation: TDD inverts traditional development: write tests before implementation. Start with simplest test case, write just enough code to pass (even hardcoded), then refactor while keeping tests green. This drives emergent design - complex algorithms evolve from simple cases. Benefits: tests provide safety net for refactoring, force consideration of edge cases early, create living documentation. Challenges: feels slower initially, requires mindset shift, can be hard for UI or when exploring new technologies. Best for well-understood domains with clear requirements.

followUps: How does TDD influence software design and architecture?
When might you choose not to use TDD for a project?
